title: LLM Security & Red Teaming
tagline: Learn how LLM apps get attacked, from prompt injection and jailbreaks to data extraction and poisoning, then test and defend your own.
prereqs: AI Engineering. AI Agents & MCP helps for the agent and tool-use steps.

steps.title: The OWASP Top 10 for LLMs
steps.why: A map of the main ways LLM applications get attacked.

steps.title: Prompt injection
steps.why: Simon Willison on why mixing instructions and untrusted text is unsafe.

steps.title: Jailbreaks
steps.why: Computerphile on how prompts talk models past their safety training.

steps.title: Automated adversarial suffixes
steps.why: Zico Kolter on optimized suffixes that jailbreak many aligned models.

steps.title: Indirect prompt injection in the wild
steps.why: Real exploits where web pages and documents hijack LLM apps.

steps.title: Extracting training data
steps.why: USENIX talk showing GPT-2 can regurgitate memorized training text.

steps.title: Backdoors and sleeper agents
steps.why: Anthropic's study of hidden trigger behavior that survived safety training.

steps.title: Design patterns for secure agents
steps.why: Limit what an agent can do after it reads untrusted input.

steps.title: Guardrails
steps.why: Add input and output rails to a chatbot with NeMo Guardrails.

steps.title: Automated red teaming with PyRIT
steps.why: Microsoft's open tool for sending attack prompts and scoring replies.

steps.title: Scan a model with garak
steps.why: Run garak's probes against your own chatbot and read the report.

steps.title: Defending against jailbreaks
steps.why: Anthropic researchers on classifier defenses and their red-teaming results.

projects: Build a small RAG chatbot, plant an indirect prompt injection in one document, and show the attack and a fix.
Run garak against a local open model and summarize which probe families succeeded.
Add an input and output safety filter to a chatbot and measure how many of 50 jailbreak prompts it blocks.
